Why was Bob confident that Jimmy would come to meet him?
questions.answer: He believed Jimmy was the truest and staunchest friend in the world, who would keep his word. He felt that if Jimmy was alive, he would surely be there.

questions.q: What was the promise made by Bob and Jimmy twenty years ago?
questions.answer: The night before Bob left for the West, they dined at 'Big Joe' Brady's and promised to meet at the same place, at ten o'clock, exactly twenty years later, whatever their condition or however far they had to travel.

questions.q: Describe the setting of the story.
questions.answer: It is ten o'clock at night on a cold, windy New York avenue with a taste of rain. The streets are almost deserted, and the shops, like the hardware store, are dark.

questions.q: How had time changed Bob and Jimmy?
questions.answer: Bob had become rich in the West by living on his wits, but he had also turned into a criminal. Jimmy had stayed in New York, become a policeman and remained honest and loyal to his duty.

questions.q: Why did Bob's hands tremble as he read the note?
questions.answer: He had expected a happy reunion, but the note told him that his friend Jimmy was the policeman who had recognised him and arranged his arrest. The shock made his hands tremble.

questions.q: What was Jimmy's inner conflict?
questions.answer: He wanted to keep faith with his old friend and his promise, but as a policeman it was his duty to arrest a wanted criminal. He chose duty, but sent another officer because he could not arrest Bob himself.

questions.q: What does the note from Jimmy reveal about his character?
questions.answer: It shows that Jimmy kept the appointment loyally, but was an honest policeman who put duty above friendship. It also shows his tenderness: he could not bear to arrest his old friend himself, so he sent a plain-clothes man and explained gently in a note.

questions.q: Bring out the surprise ending of 'After Twenty Years'.
questions.answer: We expect a happy reunion of two old friends. Instead the 'Jimmy' who arrives is a plain-clothes man who arrests Bob, and we learn that the patrolling policeman was Jimmy himself, who recognised Bob as a wanted criminal in the match-light.

or.q: Do you like the character of Bob? Give reasons.
or.answer: Bob is likable for his loyalty — he travels a thousand miles to keep a twenty-year-old promise and speaks warmly of Jimmy. But he is also boastful, showing off his watch and pin, and he has become a criminal. So he wins sympathy but not admiration.

questions.q: How does O. Henry create atmosphere in the story?
questions.answer: The cold wind, the drizzle and the nearly empty streets create a gloomy, tense mood. The dark doorway, the match-light on Bob's face and the bright drug-store lights where the truth is revealed build suspense and make the ending striking.
